newsitem.title: USA: Four added to jury pool in Broin anti-tobacco case.
newsitem.headline: Four added to jury pool in Broin anti-tobacco case.

text.p: Four potential jurors were added Wednesday to a pool from which attorneys will eventually select a panel of six people and 10 alternates to hear a landmark class-action anti-tobacco lawsuit.

The pool, which now number 100, eventually is expected to have about 125 potential jurors for a case known as Norma Broin vs. Philip Morris Cos Inc, et al., filed on behalf of thousands of flight attendants allegedly sickened by breathing secondhand cigarette smoke on U.S.-based passenger jets.
Jury selection in the case began June 2.

An attorney for Philip Morris had told the court earlier Wednesday that last week's proposed $368.5 billion settlement of scores of anti-tobacco suits would have no effect the Broin case. The lawyer, David Hardy, had flown to New York earlier this week, saying he was going to discuss the settlement's implications for the case.
